about:
# Manners

**A buff given is a favour owed. Manners, a World of Warcraft addon, repays it
in one press.**

![How Manners works, in three pictures: it picks who is missing a buff, you press one key, the buff lands and the next person in line is already waiting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fpsacha/Manners/master/.github/media/manners-how.jpg)

[![CI](https://github.com/fpsacha/Manners/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/fpsacha/Manners/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![CurseForge](https://img.shields.io/badge/CurseForge-Manners-f16436)](https://wow.curseforge.com/projects/1705364)
[![Wago](https://img.shields.io/badge/Wago-Manners-c1272d)](https://addons.wago.io/addons/rNkgzlNa)
[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Manners-5865f2)](https://discord.gg/JHc8YSDvur)
[![Licence: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-MIT-blue)](https://github.com/fpsacha/Manners/blob/master/LICENSE)

![Somebody buffed you: the prompt names Mort Defrette, who buffed you, with a mouse pointer on it and a key under it; one press, and the same prompt reads buffed Mort Defrette, the game confirmed it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fpsacha/Manners/master/.github/media/manners-prompt.png)

A priest buffs you in passing. By the time you find them among a dozen
nameplates, they are gone. Manners saw who it was and put them on one button,
*the prompt*. Press your key: they have your buff, and your own target comes
straight back.

Runs on **WoW Forever**, **Classic Era**, **Burning Crusade Classic**, **Mists
of Pandaria Classic** and **retail**, in nine languages.

## What it does for you

- **Returns a favour with one press.** Whoever buffed you, a stranger
  included, comes up on the prompt with the buff you owe them, remembered
  through a reload.
- **Your group and passers-by.** Group members missing your buff first, then
  players near you; one group cast when you carry the reagent, and top-ups
  timed to each buff.
- **Resurrection and cures** on the same button, and **courtesies** on request
  (water, portals, summons) with **Manners: Services**.
- **Asking.** A press whispers one polite line to somebody who could give you
  a buff you lack.
- **A blessing for each class.** A paladin picks the blessing each class is
  offered first.
- **Profiles that switch by themselves** for the world, dungeons, raids and
  battlegrounds, with a profile manager and *Undo*.
- **Thirty looks**, and options that start short: a Simple view and a
  painted icon for each page.
- **In character, if you like.** A line when you buff somebody, fitted to your
  race and class: the Forsaken alone have about a hundred.

Optional modules, each off until you enable it: **Combat** (one prompt that
lights up in a fight when an action you picked is needed), **My Buffs** (your
own buffs, food, flasks, scrolls and items), **Services**, **Achievements** and
**Pets** (pet care, and moments with your companion).

![Five prompts, each a different colour: your target, somebody who buffed you, somebody who asked in chat, a group member and a passer-by](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fpsacha/Manners/master/.github/media/manners-reasons.png)

## New in 1.13

- **Combat prompt**: interrupts, defensives, dispels, heals and Blessing of
  Freedom on a slowed friend, each lit only when needed; one click casts. Cards
  sit in a row (right, left, up or down) or on one spot.
- **Spells and items of my own**: add any buff spell, or an item or trinket
  whose use gives a buff, and Manners reminds you of it.
- **Achievements** that say what to do, with a goal count.
- **Companion moments**, longer right-click skips (15 to 60 minutes), a bigger
  consumables button, the Well-Rested bag before food, and Battle Shout kept to
  melee and tanks if you like.

## Installing

Install from **[Wago](https://addons.wago.io/addons/rNkgzlNa)** (and WowUp),
**[CurseForge](https://wow.curseforge.com/projects/1705364)**, or unzip a
[release](https://github.com/fpsacha/Manners/releases) into `Interface/AddOns`.
The optional modules come in the same zip and are enabled on *Choose modules*.

> **Do not install from a clone of this repository.** `Libs/` is fetched at
> build time, so a zip made from a checkout will not load. Use a release.

## The first minute

1. **See the prompt.** `/manners` opens the options on **Start here**; *Show me
   the prompt* previews it and *Move the prompt* lets you drag it.
2. **Put it on a key.** Set a key on Start here (**Options > Keybindings >
   Manners**), or press *Put Manners on an action bar* (`/manners macro`).
   A controller button works too.
3. **Stay in the Simple view** until you want more: the search box finds any
   setting.

![The prompt with a key on its chip, a row of action bar slots with the Manners macro on one showing the spell a press would cast with its cooldown sweep, and the prompt with a controller button's picture on its chip](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fpsacha/Manners/master/.github/media/manners-actionbar.png)

![The options window on Start here in the Simple view: two questions and a key for the prompt, with the Simple view switch and the Move the prompt button ringed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fpsacha/Manners/master/.github/media/manners-options.png)

## How it works

**Who comes first.** Your target, somebody who buffed you, somebody who asked
in chat, your group, then passers-by, each in its own colour. Click a name in
the prompt's list to buff that person, right-click to skip them,
shift-right-click to never offer them again.

![Click any name in the list: left-click buffs that person, right-click skips them, shift-right-click never offers them again](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fpsacha/Manners/master/.github/media/manners-list.png)

**The tooltip** says who, what and why in one line; hold Shift for everything.

![The prompt twice with its tooltip above it: the Short one with the name, the spell, why they are offered and Hold Shift for more; the Full one with Shift held, saying what the press and each click do](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fpsacha/Manners/master/.github/media/manners-tooltip.png)

**Keys, bars and controllers.** The action bar macro's first line is
`/click MannersBar`; under it Manners writes what a press would cast, so the
slot shows its icon, cooldown and range.

**In a fight** the game freezes secure buttons, so the prompt keeps what it
held at the pull and casts nothing new. The fight's own buttons (cures, Will
of the Forsaken, Mend Pet, the combat prompt) come with **Manners: Combat**.

## Your own buffs

With **Manners: My Buffs**: your armor, aura, aspect, shield or form, weapon
enhancements, food, flasks, elixirs, scrolls, tracking, the sleeping bag and a
companion pet, each with its own switch. Add any other buff spell, or an item
whose use gives a buff, under *Add a spell or an item*.

![Your own buffs on the prompt: a mage's armor, a rogue's poison for the main hand, your own Arcane Intellect](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fpsacha/Manners/master/.github/media/manners-yourself.png)

## The favour ledger

Who buffed you, what you gave back, and who you buffed first.

![The favour ledger: today's count and all-time totals, then rows of favours still owed, returned and let go, and buffs given to the group and to strangers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fpsacha/Manners/master/.github/media/manners-ledger.png)

## The prompt's look

Thirty looks, from dark glass to a death knight's runeblade, each with its
own animation, picked from a gallery of cards.

![The thirty looks for the prompt, the same favour drawn in each: Glass, the default, then Framed, Toast, Arcane, Minimal, Ghost, Hairline, Pill, Slate, Outline, Luxe, Ribbon, Letter, Warchief, Gearworks, Frost Mage, Fire Mage, Arcane Mage, Warlock, Druid, Paladin, Shaman, Death Knight, Hunter, Warrior, Priest, Rogue, Monk, Demon Hunter and Evoker](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fpsacha/Manners/master/.github/media/manners-looks.png)

![Three film strips of the prompt, four frames each: somebody buffed you, your buff lands, the game refuses it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fpsacha/Manners/master/.github/media/manners-moment.png)

![The same prompt and list in the standard reason colours and in the colour-blind friendly set](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fpsacha/Manners/master/.github/media/manners-palette.png)

## The options window

### Start here
Two questions for a new profile, a key for the prompt, the bar macro, and the
game's friendly nameplates.

### Choose modules
Turn the optional modules on and off.

### Who to buff
What to cast, on whom: favours, your group, passers-by, yourself, a blessing
for each class, Battle Shout for melee and tanks only.

### Who to skip
People left alone, the never-offer list, and how long a right-click skips.

### When to offer
Favours, top-ups, timing and targeting.

### Quiet times
Cities and inns, dungeons, battlegrounds, the mana floor, snooze.

### What I say
Thanks, the line said when you buff, In character, whispers.

### In a fight
What the prompt does when a fight starts.

### Look
The look, size, colours, sounds and the exact position.

### Profiles
Profiles that switch by themselves, and the profile manager with *Undo*.

### Diagnostics
Why the prompt is empty, the check-up and *Report a bug*.

### My own buffs
Each of your own buffs, consumables and spells or items of your own
(Manners: My Buffs).

### My companion
Your companion pet, and moments with it (Manners: Pets).

### My pet
Feed Pet, Mend Pet and pet care (Manners: Pets, hunters).

## Commands

```
/manners                    the options
/manners on | off           switch it on or off
/manners snooze [min|off]   hide the prompt for a while
/manners test | move        preview the prompt, or drag it
/manners macro              the macro for your action bar
/manners ledger             the favour ledger
/manners spell [add|remove] your own spells and items
/manners never | allow      the never-offer list
/manners export | import    share your settings
/manners debug | errors     what Manners sees, and what broke
/manners bug | mark         report a bug, or mark this moment for one
/manners selftest           check Manners against your game
/manners help               every command
```

`/mnr` works in place of `/manners`.

## Languages

![The prompt and its list in German, French and Simplified Chinese](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fpsacha/Manners/master/.github/media/manners-languages.png)

English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese,
Simplified and Traditional Chinese.

## The five clients

| Client | Version |
|---|---|
| WoW Forever | 1.60.1 |
| Classic Era, Season of Discovery included | 1.15.9 |
| Burning Crusade Classic (Anniversary) | 2.5.6 |
| Mists of Pandaria Classic | 5.5.4 |
| Retail (Midnight) | 12.1.5 |

One download holds all five, and each offers what its own game gives.

## What it cannot do, and why

- **It cannot cast by itself.** Only a key press or a click casts; Manners
  decides who and parks it on a secure button.
- **A fight freezes the button**: whoever it held at the pull stays until the
  fight ends.
- **Targeting is by name**, then your target comes back. `/target` matches the
  start of a name, so offering Mort could find Mortimer beside him; where the
  game does not say who received the spell, the favour is counted as repaid
  on the strength of the `/target` line alone.
- **It cannot see line of sight**, and sees passers-by mostly through the
  game's friendly nameplates. On WoW Forever turn those on to thank strangers.

## Troubleshooting

Press your key on the empty prompt, or read the first line of *Diagnostics*:
both say what holds it back. `/manners debug` says what Manners sees.
To report a bug press **Report a bug** (`/manners bug`): it fills in a GitHub
issue and a report to paste, with every name left out. Questions:
[Discord](https://discord.gg/JHc8YSDvur).

## For developers

Start with [CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/fpsacha/Manners/blob/master/CLAUDE.md) and [.claude/docs/](https://github.com/fpsacha/Manners/blob/master/.claude/docs);
[tests/README.md](https://github.com/fpsacha/Manners/blob/master/tests/README.md) and [tools/README.md](https://github.com/fpsacha/Manners/blob/master/tools/README.md)
explain the suites and the tools.

```
python tools/lint.py                every file compiles, the tocs are current
python tools/check.py --release     everything a release is checked against
python tools/release.py X.Y.Z       release (--dry-run prints every step)
```

`.pkgmeta` declares all 14 libraries as build-time externals.

## Licence

MIT, see `LICENSE`. Bundled libraries keep their own terms, see
`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`.

releases.notes:
*28 November 2026*

### Highlights
- **Items of my own** and **Blessing of Freedom** on a slowed friend, both off
  until you turn them on.
- The prompt works again with the Battle Shout switches on.

### Fixes
- **Battle Shout switches broke the prompt.** With *Only for melee and tanks*
  or *Only in dungeon and raid fights* on, every scan threw an error and the
  prompt stayed empty (#74).
- **Undermine Clam Chowder** gives Well Fed on WoW Forever and is offered as
  food (#73).

### New
- **Items of my own.** *Add a spell or an item* (My own buffs) takes an item
  from your bags or an equipped trinket whose use gives a buff, such as an
  Elemental Attractor (#72).
- **Blessing of Freedom** on a slowed or rooted friendly target, a paladin's
  combat action (Manners: Combat, off until you switch it on) (#71).
- **Sleeping bag before food and elixirs** (Well-Rested on My own buffs, off):
  food, flasks, elixirs and scrolls wait while the bag is due or you lie in it.

### Changes
- The README and the store pages are much shorter.

*27 November 2026*

### Highlights
- **Combat prompt** (Manners: Combat). The actions you turn on (an
  interrupt, a defensive, a hostile dispel, a heal, a mana or power
  cooldown) come up on a card only when they are needed, and one click
  casts. Each action has its own place in a short row just above the
  Manners prompt, most urgent first, so a card always appears where it
  appeared before. Every action is off until you pick it.
- **The Combat page.** Everything for a fight on one page under *Optional
  modules*: how many actions are on, *Turn all on* / *Turn all off*, the
  actions grouped by kind (each with its spell's icon), the round of the
  fight, Will of the Forsaken, the cure in a fight, Mend Pet and the
  reactive wards, and *Look and alerts*: the combat prompt's look (any look,
  tried on it as you point at it), size, pulse or strong pulse, a sound, and
  *Show and move the combat prompt* with *Reset* and *Done*.
- **More defensives found for every class**: Shield Wall, Mana Shield, Feign
  Death, Vanish, Barkskin, Power Word: Shield, Pain Suppression and Blessing
  of Protection, each listed once.
- **My companion** (Manners: Pets, any class with a pet journal). With
  *Moments with my companion* on (off by default), now and then a moment
  with the pet that follows you: hello when it comes out, well done after a
  long fight, a pat on the road, a game when you stand still, a celebration
  when you level up, a cuddle at an inn or a city, a hug back from the dead
  and a treat for a quest. Each has its own switch; the gestures and its
  answers vary, and with In character on something sweet is said to it.
  `/manners debug` and the check-up show the moment waiting.
- **Achievements** on a page of their own, drawn as a board: your rank and
  points, what you earned lately, tabs by kind, by progress and by order,
  and a card for each achievement that says what to do, which goal it works
  toward, such as Goal 2 of 3, and the count. Old saves keep their counts.

### Changes
- **Where the combat cards sit** (Combat, Look and alerts): *A row* that grows
  right, left, up or down from your spot, or *One spot* where every card shows
  in the same place, the most urgent on top.
- **Longer skips for your own buffs.** *After a right-click on my own buff,
  offer 15, 30, 45 or 60 minutes* (Who to skip, off) puts four small buttons
  under the prompt after a right-click on your own buff (#69).
- **Consumables button** is bigger (48), shows the item's name under it, and
  has *Show and move the consumables button* on My own buffs: a named bar,
  *Reset* and *Done*, dragged with the prompt locked.
- **Ask waits half a minute.** Nobody is offered as an ask until they have
  stayed within reach thirty seconds, so a group that just met is not asked
  at once.
- **Your own buff is not held into a fight.** The prompt no longer stays on
  you all fight as *held -- in combat*; with nobody else to offer it goes
  before the fight. A warrior's shout still stays.
- **Outline look** repainted: a flat bar with a hard black edge and a soft
  shadow, a square socket for the icon, and no seam where its pieces meet.
- **Options window.** The page's sections are real tabs; the optional
  modules come first under *Choose modules*, each page with the game's own
  icon; a switch that names a spell shows that spell's icon.

### Fixes
- **Ask people for a buff I'm missing** with Proximity on *Anywhere I can
  cast* asks people in sight again (#68).
- **Cozy Sleeping Bag** on Classic Era goes down at your feet in one press;
  a second press never placed it (#70).
- **Combat actions on yourself** (Shield Block, Ice Block, Evasion and the
  like) on WoW Forever get their macro.
- **Combat prompt clicks.** The game does not let an addon change which
  button is on top in a fight, so the cards are never stacked: the needed
  one always takes the click.

*27 November 2026*

### Highlights
- **Battle Shout recipients.** Off by default, warriors can limit Battle Shout
  reminders to tanks and reliably identified melee players, with a separate
  choice to show them only in combat inside dungeons and raids.

### Fixes
- **Combat and module toggles on Forever.** Shared Combat buttons now pass
  both dimensions to the client, and Manners uses the player's GUID for the
  addon's per-character enable state, so switches and module pages agree after
  Reload UI.
- **Own food remains authoritative.** A secret or refused meal-aura read no
  longer lets a second food prompt interrupt an active meal.
- **Failed service delivery stays pending.** A blocked healthstone or Soulstone
  trade no longer consumes the request, and outside-instance service rules do
  not fail open when the client's instance answer is unreadable.
- **New requests replace stale ones.** A recognised request filtered during
  combat clears the sender's older pending intent instead of leaving it to be
  served later.
- **Reactive wards must be castable.** A ward button appears only when the
  matching spell is known, usable, funded and off cooldown.
- **Module chooser and migration state are safer.** The one-time chooser belongs
  to the profile that scheduled it, retries if it was not shown, and shared
  profiles reconcile modules per character without overriding an explicit off.
- **A press settles only its own cast.** A secret spell ID from an unrelated
  cast can no longer clear a favour or consume a request.

*27 November 2026*

### Highlights
- **All optional modules start on.** Combat, My Buffs, Services, Pets and
  Achievements are enabled in a new install. The first login after 1.12.5
  opens one explanation and chooser; saved user-off module choices remain off.
- **Existing module choices are restored.** Profiles from before optional
  modules enable the folders their saved My Buffs, Services or Combat settings
  need, once, without turning anything on for a new or intentionally-off profile.
- **Outline.** A thirtieth look, a clean near-black prompt with a crisp black
  outline and a square spell socket, is now available under Look.
- **Reactive wards on classic clients.** Classic Era and TBC can show a
  pre-armed Fire Ward or Frost Ward secure button after a concrete matching
  damage event. The option is off by default; clients that withhold combat
  values do not guess.

### Changes
- **Module switches.** An unloaded module can be enabled for the next reload
  during combat; a loaded module cannot be suspended while protected frames
  are locked.
- **Class colours.** Dark prompts use the game's exact class colours instead of
  lightened tints. A light-ground look still adjusts them only as needed to
  keep the name readable.

### Fixes
- **Will of the Forsaken for Sleep.** The loss-of-control event's index is read
  and a briefly empty result is rechecked safely, while a plainly reported
  stun still does not spend the racial cooldown.
- **Own buffs and services survive the split.** Rogue poisons and stones, Druid
  self-buffs including Thorns, and saved Mage service requests are restored by
  enabling My Buffs or Services for existing profiles.
- **Keyboard control in Settings.** Closing or losing the options window now
  releases key capture, so WASD and Escape return to the game.
- **Combat-module teardown.** Delayed CureFight, Mend Pet and BreakFree
  callbacks stop after Combat is switched off or suspended.
- **Favour settlement race.** A delayed cast can no longer clear a newer favour
  that replaced the debt which the press originally answered.
- **Withheld own-spell range.** A secret range result is no longer treated as
  proof that an own spell cannot target the player.

### Reliability
- **Package and test gates.** A killed scenario worker, missing package job or
  dead TOC, XML or library reference now fails validation instead of passing a
  structural package.

*27 November 2026*

### Highlights
- **Optional modules load cleanly.** The binding XML and the reload action are
  fixed in a small hotfix for 1.12.3.

### Fixes
- **Optional-module bindings.** Manners: My Buffs and Manners: Combat no longer
  load their `Bindings.xml` twice, which caused WoW Forever to report
  `Unrecognized XML: Binding` when a module was enabled.
- **Module reload feedback.** The Optional modules page now puts *Reload now*
  before the module list, so a switch change immediately shows what must be
  pressed to apply it.
